title: Orizon Agents: evidence index for the Stellar Instaward

sow.note: This index follows the approved SOW v4, dated 2026-08-01. Section 6.1 says what evidence each deliverable owes, section 6.2 is the checklist the Ambassador Chapter Lead marks (Present, Partial or Missing), and section 6.3 lists the eleven success metrics. Each deliverable below repeats the SOW's Evidence Type and Description word for word. Every piece of evidence has a status and a link you can open, and anything missing or partly done says why in plain words.

snapshot.method: Every on-chain link was re-read on 2026-09-29 from Stellar's public testnet record (Horizon, horizon-testnet.stellar.org). Each transaction was confirmed successful, and the date beside it is the day the ledger recorded it, in UTC. Contract activity was cross-checked on Stellar Expert. Every web link was opened without logging in and returned a working page. A wallet counts as the team's when it is in the team wallet register (backend repository, app/data/team_wallets.json) or holds a platform role on the contracts. Nothing was signed, paid or submitted to make this snapshot.

deliverables.name: Permissionless Agent Registration
deliverables.evidence_type: Repo PR(s) · live URL · tx hash
deliverables.sow_text: Merged PRs for the registration flow, the live "Register an Agent" URL on the deployed dApp, and an externally owned agent's registration tx hash on Stellar Expert (testnet).

items.claim: The registration flow is built and merged: the Register an Agent page, signing in the operator's own wallet, and the backend endpoints that build, check and list a registration.
items.note: The contract's register call was already open to any wallet. Story 1.01 audited it and needed no contract change, so there is no contracts pull request for this item.

deliverables.name: Reputation-Gated Routing
deliverables.sow_text: A short recording/screenshots of the decompose plan card showing on-chain reputation per agent, plus a routing example where a sub-floor agent is excluded, and a link to the routing code.

items.claim: Screenshots or a recording of the plan card showing each agent's on-chain reputation before the buyer pays.
items.note: Partial. A screenshot of the live plan card exists, taken on 2026-09-19. It shows a reputation score on every step and the 2.75 routing floor. But every agent in it still had the starting estimate (about 3.50 out of 5), not a score earned on-chain, because the platform only began writing ratings later that day. No recording exists yet. Since then the platform has written 27 ratings on-chain, two of which are linked here, so the live plan card now shows earned scores for rated agents. Those ratings came from live test runs whose payments did not settle (see the disclosures). A new screenshot or recording would make this item present.

items.claim: A routing example where an agent below the reputation floor is left out of the plan.
items.note: Missing. No agent on the live registry is below the floor today, so there is no live exclusion to show. The lowest is the team's test agent uat624_ext_op, with an on-chain average of about 2.07 out of 5. But every agent starts from an estimate of 3.50, and a few small test ratings are not yet enough evidence to pull it under the 2.75 floor. The exclusion logic is merged and tested (the pull requests here, and the code in the next item). The only frame showing an exclusion so far used a plan written by a test, so it is not offered as evidence. This item becomes present with a recording of a live plan that leaves out a below-floor agent.

links.label: Backend pull request #51: the plan lists any agent the floor left out, and the floor itself (merged)

items.claim: A link to the routing code that applies the reputation floor.
items.note: The code links are pinned to the backend merge of 2026-09-18 (pull request #58), when this routing shipped. The floor check itself is unchanged in the later build the live API runs. The floor is judged on a cautious lower estimate of each agent's on-chain average, so a new agent with few ratings is not over-trusted or over-punished.
